transcript: I don't understand that. I'm actually really frustrated by the fact that we have started reverting to incomplete cast albums. This used to happen all the time in the 50s, 60s, and 70s. Because you had to mass market cast albums for vinyl records. And vinyl records had a very strict time constraint about how much you could fit onto a single vinyl record. And so they would shorten all of the cast albums. They would even speed up some of the songs sometimes for specifically the album. But then in the 90s and 2000s we started getting complete versions of these cast albums for the first time ever. Because you no longer had those time constraints. We were starting to shift to digital music or to C DS that were a lot cheaper to produce. And so we got complete albums for the first time ever. Like. Like the deluxe edition of Follies that had all of the cut tracks that had ever been written for Follies. Like, that was. That was a treat. And now we've reverted back to incomplete cast albums. Where we're losing things like scenes and transitions. And I wonder. I wonder how much of it, of course, is money. And the fact that it is more expensive to produce Broadway shows than ever before. And that includes paying everybody for the album. But I also wonder how much of it is because people don't sit down and listen to albums anymore. People add Songs to playlist, myself included. We add our favourite songs to playlist and we're more likely to add songs that don't have all of the added dialogue. But it just feels. It feels like we're losing something in this process. And it's so. It's so frustrating to me that we don't have a complete cast album of this ragtime revival. And I have a lot of thoughts on the ragtime album as a whole, and those will come at a later time. But my biggest frustrating is. My biggest frustration is why. Why did we not just cut the scenes and the transitions, but, like, full songs? Like, why did they cut Atlantic City? I don't understand. Like, that's a song. That's a full song. Is it the best song in the show? No, but the fact that it's not on this album is just weird. Like, it's not like a spoilery song either. Like wicked witch of the east anyway. I have a lot of frustrations, but that's. That's my biggest one is why. Why are albums from the 90s and 2000s more complete than albums of today? And why do they sound better anyway?
